details.description: GPT-4o mini TTS is OpenAI's text-to-speech model built on GPT-4o mini, converting written text into spoken audio through the Speech API (/v1/audio/speech). It offers 13 built-in voices (alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, fable, nova, onyx, sage, shimmer, verse, marin and cedar) and can be instructed, via a text prompt, to control accent, emotion, intonation, pacing, tone and whispering. OpenAI describes it as its newest and most reliable text-to-speech model, ahead of the older tts-1 and tts-1-hd models, and recommends the marin or cedar voices for the best quality. OpenAI's text-to-speech guide lists 57 supported languages, following the Whisper model's language coverage, though its voices are optimized for English.
advantages: Offers 13 built-in voices, more than the 9 voices on OpenAI's older tts-1 and tts-1-hd models, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
Accepts natural-language prompt instructions to control accent, emotion, intonation, pacing, tone and whispering, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
Supports realtime audio streaming via chunked transfer encoding, letting playback start before the full audio file is generated, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
Supports 57 languages, following the Whisper model's language coverage, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
disadvantages: Voices are optimized for English even though the model follows Whisper's broader language coverage, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
Limited to the Speech Generation endpoint; does not support chat completions, fine-tuning or other API endpoints, per OpenAI's model page.
Text input is limited to 2,000 tokens per request, per OpenAI's model page.
use_cases: Narrating written blog posts and articles as spoken audio, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
Producing multilingual spoken audio output, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.
Realtime voice output for conversational or interactive applications via audio streaming, per OpenAI's text-to-speech guide.

notes: OpenAI's model page and text-to-speech guide describe gpt-4o-mini-tts as text-in/audio-out only (no audio input), which conflicts with the catalog's audio_input modality fact; kept the catalog's modality as instructed. OpenAI's deprecations page does not list gpt-4o-mini-tts, unlike the catalog's 2027-06-15 deprecation_date, so that date could not be confirmed from a source. The text-to-speech guide's 'Supported languages' section names 57 languages for this model (not '100+' as originally written); the languages field now lists them and the description/advantages were corrected to match.
